condition: subacute nummular coin shaped itchy eczema plaques on shins failing plain moisturizer
level_rationale: Coin-shaped red skin patches on both shins that appeared 3 weeks ago in a 46-year-old adult and have remained dry and itchy despite daily plain moisturizing lotion represent subacute emollient-refractory lower-extremity dermatitis requiring an outpatient general-physician visit for diagnosis and prescription topical corticosteroid therapy rather than continued home lotion alone or emergency care, whereas coin-shaped red patches on both shins from 3 weeks ago that cleared up completely after daily plain lotion represent resolved dry skin needing only routine home self-care.
